items.stem: After an alcohol-related conviction, what bar does an Alcohol Restricted Driver face?

options.text: One drink per hour while driving
options.rationale: Wrong: the bar is zero alcohol, not a paced amount.

options.text: No alcohol at all in the body while driving
options.rationale: The handbook bars any alcohol in the body for this driver.

options.text: Only beer and wine while driving
options.rationale: Wrong: no beverage type is excepted.

options.text: Alcohol only on weekends while driving
options.rationale: Wrong: no day of the week is excepted.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: the handbook bars any alcohol in the body for this driver.

items.stem: What proof can establish Extreme DUI?

options.text: Any detectable alcohol at all
options.rationale: Wrong: mere detectability is the restricted-driver rule, not Extreme DUI.

options.text: Two prior DUIs within 5 years
options.rationale: Wrong: priors are not part of the Extreme DUI test.

options.text: At least sixteen hundredths alcohol, or five hundredths with a controlled substance, or two combined uncontrolled substances
options.rationale: Extreme DUI turns on high readings or drug combinations, not on history or refusal.

options.text: Refusing the breath test twice
options.rationale: Wrong: refusal is not one of the three prongs.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: Extreme DUI turns on high readings or drug combinations, not on history or refusal.

items.stem: What does an Ignition Interlock Device do?

options.text: It locks the steering wheel when parked
options.rationale: Wrong: no steering lock is involved.

options.text: It alerts police after any traffic stop
options.rationale: Wrong: no police alert is involved.

options.text: It records speed for the insurance company
options.rationale: Wrong: no speed recording is involved.

options.text: It monitors breath alcohol before the vehicle can start or keep running
options.rationale: The device is a constant breath-test monitor tied to starting and operating.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: the device is a constant breath-test monitor tied to starting and operating.

items.stem: Who counts as an interdicted person?

options.text: Anyone barred by law or court order from being furnished alcohol
options.rationale: Interdiction is a legal ban on furnishing alcohol to the person.

options.text: Anyone who holds a commercial license
options.rationale: Wrong: holding a commercial license is unrelated.

options.text: Anyone under twenty-one who drives
options.rationale: Wrong: age alone does not interdict anyone.

options.text: Anyone who failed the written test
options.rationale: Wrong: test failure does not interdict anyone.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: interdiction is a legal ban on furnishing alcohol to the person.

items.stem: What must an Interlock Restricted Driver do?

options.text: Drive only during daylight hours
options.rationale: Wrong: no daylight limit applies.

options.text: Drive only a vehicle with an installed ignition interlock
options.rationale: The restriction requires the installed interlock system in the driven vehicle.

options.text: Drive only with a licensed adult beside them
options.rationale: Wrong: no supervising adult is required.

options.text: Drive only vehicles with manual transmissions
options.rationale: Wrong: no transmission type is required.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: the restriction requires the installed interlock system in the driven vehicle.

items.stem: How does Alcohol Restricted status differ from Extreme DUI?

options.text: Restricted status is stricter than Extreme DUI in every case
options.rationale: Wrong: neither label outranks the other; they measure different things.

options.text: Extreme DUI applies only to commercial drivers
options.rationale: Wrong: no commercial-only limit applies to Extreme DUI.

options.text: Restricted status is a zero-alcohol bar after past offenses; Extreme DUI is a present offense tier
options.rationale: One is a driver status from history, the other is an offense tier from current readings.

options.text: The two terms mean exactly the same thing
options.rationale: Wrong: status and offense tier are distinct ideas.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: one is a driver status from history, the other is an offense tier from current readings.

items.stem: How do the interlock driver rule, the interdicted rule, and the IID differ?

options.text: All three require jail time
options.rationale: Wrong: no jail term is stated for any of them.

options.text: All three apply only to repeat felons
options.rationale: Wrong: no felony history is required.

options.text: All three ban driving for life
options.rationale: Wrong: no lifetime ban is stated.

options.text: The restricted driver needs the device installed, the interdicted person gets no alcohol, and the IID is the hardware
options.rationale: Driver restriction, furnishing ban, and breath-test hardware are three separate things.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: driver restriction, furnishing ban, and breath-test hardware are three separate things.

items.stem: When is a license cancelled?

options.text: When it was issued through error or fraud, or consent was withdrawn
options.rationale: Cancellation targets bad issuance and withdrawn consent.

options.text: After any single speeding ticket
options.rationale: Wrong: a single ticket is not a cancellation trigger.

options.text: After the driver turns seventy
options.rationale: Wrong: no age trigger applies.

options.text: When the driver moves to a new county
options.rationale: Wrong: a move is not a cancellation trigger.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: cancellation targets bad issuance and withdrawn consent.

items.stem: What does denied mean?

options.rationale: Wrong: photo quality is unrelated.

options.text: The driving privilege has been withdrawn
options.rationale: Denial withdraws the privilege itself.

options.text: The test appointment was cancelled
options.rationale: Wrong: scheduling is unrelated.

options.text: The renewal fee went unpaid
options.rationale: Wrong: payment is unrelated.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: denial withdraws the privilege itself.

items.stem: What is disqualification, and whose license does it touch?

options.text: Temporary withdrawal of any regular license
options.rationale: Wrong: regular licenses are outside this definition.

options.text: A fine for parking violations
options.rationale: Wrong: no fine is involved.

options.text: Temporary or permanent withdrawal of a commercial driver license
options.rationale: Disqualification is commercial-license only.

options.text: A warning letter from the Division
options.rationale: Wrong: no warning letter is involved.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: disqualification is commercial-license only.

items.stem: What is revocation?

options.text: A pause of the privilege for thirty days
options.rationale: Wrong: no fixed-day pause is stated.

options.text: A restriction to daylight driving
options.rationale: Wrong: no daylight limit is stated.

options.text: A fee added to renewal
options.rationale: Wrong: no fee is stated.

options.text: Termination of the privilege to drive
options.rationale: Revocation ends the privilege outright.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: revocation ends the privilege outright.

items.stem: What is suspension?

options.text: Temporary withdrawal of the privilege to drive
options.rationale: Suspension is temporary, not terminal.

options.text: Permanent loss of the privilege
options.rationale: Wrong: permanence belongs to revocation, not suspension.

options.text: Loss of vehicle registration
options.rationale: Wrong: registration is a separate matter.

options.text: Seizure of the license plates
options.rationale: Wrong: plates are a separate matter.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: suspension is temporary, not terminal.

items.stem: How do cancellation and denied differ?

options.text: Cancellation hits privilege; denied hits the document
options.rationale: Wrong: the direction is exactly reversed.

options.text: Cancellation ends a wrongly issued license; denied withdraws the privilege
options.rationale: One ends the document, the other withdraws the right.

options.text: Both mean the same permanent loss
options.rationale: Wrong: neither is defined as permanent here.

options.text: Both apply only to commercial licenses
options.rationale: Wrong: no commercial-only limit applies.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: one ends the document, the other withdraws the right.

items.stem: How do suspension and revocation differ?

options.text: Suspension is permanent; revocation is brief
options.rationale: Wrong: the pairing is exactly reversed.

options.text: Both are permanent losses
options.rationale: Wrong: suspension is defined as temporary.

options.text: Suspension withdraws privilege temporarily; revocation ends it
options.rationale: Temporary versus outright is the whole difference.

options.text: Both are thirty-day pauses
options.rationale: Wrong: no fixed-day pause is stated for either.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: temporary versus outright is the whole difference.

items.stem: Who assumes financial responsibility for an applicant?

options.text: Any licensed driver over eighteen
options.rationale: Wrong: mere licensure is not enough.

options.text: The driving examiner
options.rationale: Wrong: the examiner never assumes it.

options.text: The vehicle seller
options.rationale: Wrong: the seller never assumes it.

options.text: A parent, guardian, or willing responsible adult
options.rationale: A parent, guardian, or willing responsible adult takes the obligation.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: a parent, guardian, or willing responsible adult takes the obligation.

items.stem: Who counts as a dependent?

options.text: A spouse and unmarried children under twenty-one
options.rationale: Spouse plus unmarried children under twenty-one.

options.text: Any relative living nearby
options.rationale: Wrong: mere kinship is not enough.

options.text: Parents and grandparents only
options.rationale: Wrong: the definition names spouse and children, not parents.

options.text: Married children under twenty-five
options.rationale: Wrong: married children are excluded and the age is twenty-one.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: spouse plus unmarried children under twenty-one.

options.text: The vehicle emissions bureau

options.text: The insurance policy

items.stem: What is a license certificate?

options.text: The driving test score sheet

options.text: The vehicle title

options.text: The document evidencing the privilege to drive

items.stem: Who is an operator?

options.text: Whoever owns the vehicle
options.rationale: Wrong: ownership without control is not operation.

options.text: Whoever sits in the back seat

options.text: Whoever pays the insurance

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: operation is actual physical control.

items.stem: How do license, certificate, and operator relate?

options.rationale: Right, paper, and person must not be merged.

options.text: Only the operator needs any of them
options.rationale: Wrong: the license and certificate exist apart from any operator.

options.text: Only commercial drivers use them

options.text: Ones rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or built for sixteen-plus passengers or special cargo
options.rationale: Weight, passenger capacity, or cargo triggers the CDL.

options.text: Any vehicle driven on Sundays
options.rationale: Wrong: the day of the week is irrelevant.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: weight, passenger capacity, or cargo triggers the CDL.

options.text: Division authority with conditions for driving a mobility vehicle on public highways
options.rationale: Division authority plus conditions for highway driving.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: Division authority plus conditions for highway driving.

items.stem: What caps define a pedestrian vehicle?

options.text: No more than forty-eight inches wide, no engine over three hundred cubic centimeters or twelve brake horsepower, under thirty miles per hour
options.rationale: Width, engine, and speed caps all bind.

options.text: 80 inches wide with a 500 cc engine at 60 mph
options.rationale: Wrong: every figure there exceeds the stated caps.

options.text: No caps of any kind
options.rationale: Wrong: the caps are the whole point.

options.text: Only a color requirement
options.rationale: Wrong: color is never mentioned.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: width, engine, and speed caps all bind.

items.stem: What is a personal motorized mobility device?

options.text: A three-wheeled motorcycle
options.rationale: Wrong: three wheels break the definition.

options.text: A self-propelled two-wheel non-tandem device with steering, stopping, a one-horsepower motor, and a stand-on deck
options.rationale: Two non-tandem wheels, steering, stopping, small motor, stand-on deck.

options.text: A car with hand controls
options.rationale: Wrong: cars are a different class.

options.text: A bicycle with a basket
options.rationale: Wrong: baskets and pedals are not in the definition.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: two non-tandem wheels, steering, stopping, small motor, stand-on deck.

items.stem: How do the mobility vehicle and its permit differ?

options.text: They are the same document
options.rationale: Wrong: one is equipment, the other is authority.

options.text: The permit is the vehicle itself
options.rationale: Wrong: the permit grants driving, it is not driven.

options.text: The vehicle meets Division specs; the permit is the Division authority with conditions
options.rationale: Equipment versus authority.

options.text: Neither involves the Division
options.rationale: Wrong: the Division specs the vehicle and issues the permit.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: equipment versus authority.

items.stem: How do pedestrian vehicles and mobility devices differ?

options.text: Both carry identical caps
options.rationale: Wrong: only the pedestrian vehicle is capped.

options.text: Neither has any definition
options.rationale: Wrong: both are defined terms.

options.text: The device is always larger
options.rationale: Wrong: no size ranking is stated.

options.text: Both serve limited mobility, but only the pedestrian vehicle carries the width, engine, and speed caps
options.rationale: Shared purpose, one-sided caps.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: shared purpose, one-sided caps.

items.stem: What are blind spots?

options.text: Roadway areas unseen in the mirrors while operating the vehicle
options.rationale: Mirror-unseen roadway during operation.

options.text: Areas behind the sun visor
options.rationale: Wrong: visors are unrelated.

options.text: The dashboard warning lights
options.rationale: Wrong: warning lights are unrelated.

options.text: Rest stops along the highway
options.rationale: Wrong: rest stops are unrelated.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: mirror-unseen roadway during operation.

items.stem: What makes driving careless?

options.text: One parking ticket
options.rationale: Wrong: parking tickets are not moving violations.

options.text: Two or more moving violations in one continuous drive, or one violation plus unrelated in-vehicle distraction
options.rationale: Repeated violations in one drive, or one violation plus unrelated distraction.

options.text: Driving exactly at the speed limit
options.rationale: Wrong: obeying the limit is the opposite of careless.

options.text: Wearing a seat belt
options.rationale: Wrong: belts are unrelated to the triggers.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: repeated violations in one drive, or one violation plus unrelated distraction.

items.stem: What is a head check?

options.text: Staring straight ahead only
options.rationale: Wrong: straight-ahead gaze misses the blind spot.

options.text: Closing the eyes briefly
options.rationale: Wrong: closing the eyes abandons all checks.

options.text: Glancing over the shoulder toward the intended move to cover the blind spot
options.rationale: Shoulder glance toward the move covering the blind spot.

options.text: Reading a map while moving
options.rationale: Wrong: map reading is itself a distraction.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: shoulder glance toward the move covering the blind spot.

items.stem: What is a traffic check?

options.text: A check of the fuel gauge
options.rationale: Wrong: gauges are unrelated.

options.text: A check of tire pressure
options.rationale: Wrong: tires are unrelated.

options.text: A check of the radio station
options.rationale: Wrong: radios are unrelated.

options.text: A defensive scan for nearby traffic, pedestrians, and other obstacles
options.rationale: Defensive scan for traffic, people, and obstacles.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: defensive scan for traffic, people, and obstacles.

items.stem: What are the two independent careless-driving triggers?

options.text: Repeated moving violations in one drive, or one violation plus unrelated distraction
options.rationale: Either trigger alone makes careless driving.

options.text: Two flat tires in one trip
options.rationale: Wrong: mechanical trouble is not a trigger.

options.text: Two passengers talking at once
options.rationale: Wrong: passengers alone are not a trigger.

options.text: Two red lights in a row
options.rationale: Wrong: obeying signals is the opposite of careless.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: either trigger alone makes careless driving.
